items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: we were such close friends as kids

ctx.x:
I never forgot that, you know.
But the Italians, they lived in that district, but they usually were on a section all by themselves over there. Uh-huh. But some strange things happened in the South in those days because I grew up with some Italian kids, and we got to be real good friends. And they were the Rekuparos. And, in fact, their father had a grocery store. And they couldn't -- they could just barely speak English, the father and the mother.

And these kids and I would play together all the time. And one of these kinds, Frankie Rekuparo, we were such close friends as kids until he wanted to go to theater with me, and that was kind of taboo down South in those days. And Frankie -- we were kids, just young kids. And I worked for his father's grocery store delivering groceries. But they would help me deliver the groceries.

By anyway, one day I took Frankie and I put some charcoal dust all over his face -- I never forgot this when he was a little kid -- because he wanted to see a movie that was at the colored theater, the Star Theater at West Broad Street. And this was a picture with Tom Mix in it. I never forgot that. We loved cowboys, you know, in those days.
